The space of degree-$d$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^n$ is parametrized by nonzero homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in $n+1$ variables, modulo scaling. The vector space of such polynomials has dimension

$$\dim H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, \mathcal{O}(d)) = \binom{d+n}{d}.$$

Hence the parameter space of degree-$d$ hypersurfaces is $\mathbb{P}^{\binom{d+n}{d}-1}$.

**Imposing a point condition.** Requiring a hypersurface to pass through a fixed point $p \in \mathbb{P}^n$ is a single linear condition on the coefficients of the defining polynomial (evaluate the polynomial at $p$ and set it to $0$). Thus each point imposes one linear equation on the $\binom{d+n}{d}$-dimensional vector space of forms.

**Generic independence.** A standard fact from interpolation theory: $r$ points in generic position impose independent conditions on forms of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ whenever $r \leq \binom{d+n}{d}$. Concretely, the evaluation map

$$H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, \mathcal{O}(d)) \longrightarrow \mathbb{C}^r, \qquad F \mapsto (F(p_1),\dots,F(p_r))$$

is surjective for generic $p_1,\dots,p_r$ when $r \leq \binom{d+n}{d}$. This can be seen by induction on $r$: a generic point avoids any fixed proper linear subspace of the target, so each new generic point adds an independent condition. (Equivalently, the locus where the evaluation map drops rank is a proper closed subset, so its complement is nonempty.)

**Applying the count.** Here the number of points is

$$r = \binom{d+n}{d} - 1 \;<\; \binom{d+n}{d},$$

so the conditions are independent. The kernel of the evaluation map — the space of degree-$d$ forms vanishing at all $r$ generic points — has dimension

$$\binom{d+n}{d} - r = \binom{d+n}{d} - \left(\binom{d+n}{d}-1\right) = 1.$$

A one-dimensional vector space of forms corresponds, modulo scaling, to a **single** hypersurface. (The unique nonzero form in this 1-dim space is not the zero polynomial, since the zero polynomial does not define a hypersurface; the 1-dim space is spanned by a genuine nonzero form.)

Therefore, the number of degree-$d$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^n$ containing a generic set of $\binom{d+n}{d}-1$ points is

$$\boxed{1}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
